topics.title: The church modes, hexachords and the road to major/minor

attachTo.note: Fux writes in the modes (fux.json → modes). Show this as background beside the mode list.

rules.text: The four finals are D, E, F, G (protus, deuterus, tritus, tetrardus); each has an authentic and a plagal mode.
Authentic modes range about an octave above the final; plagal modes from a fourth below to a fifth above.
Mi–fa is always the semitone; the syllables ut re mi fa sol la name a hexachord T–T–S–T–T.
The mode of a polyphonic work is judged chiefly from its tenor: final, range, species and cadences.
There are twelve modes: the eight church modes plus Aeolian and Hypoaeolian on A, Ionian and Hypoionian on C.
A hexachord has the pattern ut re mi fa sol la (T–T–S–T–T) and stands on C (natural), G (hard, with b♮) or F (soft, with b♭).

guidelines.text: Each mode suits certain words and affects (e.g., mode 2 tearful, mode 5 joyful).

topics.title: Before species: organum, discant and contrapunctus

rules.text: In organum at the fourth, the organal voice may not descend below the boundary tone; it holds that tone and converges to the unison at phrase ends.
Concords: perfect = unison, octave; medial = fifth, fourth; imperfect = major and minor third.
rules.who: Johannes de Garlandia, De mensurabili musica (c. 1250)

rules.text: Begin and end on a perfect consonance; never move in parallel perfect consonances of the same kind.
An imperfect consonance must move to the nearest perfect consonance: major sixth to octave, major third to fifth, minor third to unison.

terms.def: Early polyphony: a voice added to chant by rule.
The convergence of the organal voice onto the principal voice at a cadence.
Measured note-against-note polyphony of the 13th century.
"Note against note": the 14th-century system of consonant two-voice writing.
Notes outside the gamut (added sharps and flats), e.g., to perfect a cadence.

rules.text: All concords must be used; begin and end with perfect concords; avoid successive perfect concords of the same kind; prefer contrary motion; seek variety.

rules.text: Dissonance is allowed in florid counterpoint only on unaccented parts of the beat or as a syncopation prepared and resolved down by step.

attachTo.note: The four rules of motion predate Fux (Zarlino 1558).

rules.text: From perfect to perfect consonance: contrary or oblique motion.
From perfect to imperfect consonance: any motion.
From imperfect to perfect consonance: contrary or oblique motion.
From imperfect to imperfect consonance: any motion.
Two perfect consonances of the same kind in succession are forbidden.

tools.title: Mode explorer (8 and 12 modes)
tools.spec: Choose a mode (1–8, or Glarean 9–12). Show final, ambitus, reciting tone (tenor of the psalm tone), species of fifth + fourth, Greek name (Alia musica tradition) and Zarlino's 1571 renumbering. Draw the octave with final and tenor marked; play the scale and a short typical cadence.
tests: Mode 1: final D, ambitus D–d, tenor A
Mode 2: final D, ambitus A–a, tenor F

tools.title: Gamut & hexachord solmizer
tools.spec: Draw the Guidonian gamut Γ-ut to e-la (G2–E5) with all syllables per step. Input a melody of letter names (with b for b♭). Output syllables with mutations marked: stay in the current hexachord when possible; mutate at the latest common note before leaving its range; b♭ forces the soft (F) hexachord, b♮ the hard (G). Show cantus durus/mollis. Play the melody.
tests: C D E F G A → ut re mi fa sol la (natural)
G A B C D E F (b♮) → mutation to natural hexachord on D or E: ut re mi fa (hard) … la in natural
F G A Bb → ut re mi fa (soft)

tools.title: Organum & contrapunctus lab
tools.spec: Input a chant (letters). Modes: parallel organum at the octave / fifth / composite (four voices); organum at the fourth with boundary tone (organal voice may not go below the tritus C below; holds it; converges to the unison at the end — occursus). Under every vertical interval show Garlandia's class (perfect / medial / imperfect concord or discord). A "contrapunctus check" flags parallel perfect consonances and imperfect→perfect moves that do not go to the nearest perfect consonance.
tests: Organum at the fourth never goes below the boundary tone
P5 → P5 in parallel motion is flagged in contrapunctus mode
